2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = the GROUP BY column
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the TUMBLE size, in seconds. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: PERIOD — the HOP slide, in seconds. PERIOD = 60
11 // primitive: GAP — the SESSION gap, in seconds. GAP = 120
12 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
13 // primitive: KEYS — the distinct GROUP BY values. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
14 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
15 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those row ids.
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest et through i, minus LAG.
22 // primitive: J — the join window: rows match if their et are within J seconds. J = 60
23 // primitive: rowsOf(key) — one side of the join.
25 // primitive: absDiff(a, b) — the distance between two times. absDiff(1, 50) = 49
27 // function: sideWatermark(key, i) — one input's own completeness claim after row i.
33 if (seen == NONE || EVENTS[j].et > seen) { seen = EVENTS[j].et }
39 // function: joinWatermark(i) — the MINIMUM over inputs. A side that has produced
40 // nothing blocks the claim entirely: silence is not completeness.
47 if (lowest == NONE || w < lowest) { lowest = w }
52 // function: matches(clock) — every pair within J on the chosen clock. The clock
53 // decides WHICH ROWS ARE PAIRED, not just which bucket a value lands in.
60 if (absDiff(l[clock], r[clock]) <= J) { out = append(out, [l.id, r.id]) }
66 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the claim, and the pairings under both clocks.
Step 3/0 — the clock decides WHICH ROWS ARE PAIRED
`absDiff(1, 50)` = 49, within J = 60, so the pair is emitted. Note what this line asserts about the world: these two things happened close together. A wrong
clock here does not mis-bucket a number, it states a false coincidence.
